column1: # Fonts the app ships, fetched at build time and never committed.
# The handheld's rootfs installs `fonts-noto-cjk` and nothing else — no Latin
# face at all. EmulationStation papered over that by fetching Android's
# DroidSansFallbackFull itself; strip ES and the gap is ours. So these are the
# scripts CJK does not cover, and they come to about 2.3 MB.
# CJK is not in the default set, and that is a decision rather than an
# oversight. Both targets already have it:
#   * the handheld installs `fonts-noto-cjk` — one NotoSansCJK-Regular.ttc
#     holding the JP, KR, SC, TC and HK faces, which the font database reads
#     out separately, so asking for "Noto Sans CJK TC" by name works there;
#   * macOS ships Hiragino, PingFang SC and PingFang TC.
# and it is 50 MB against the 2.3 MB of everything above. Where a machine
# turns out to lack it the app says so at startup rather than drawing boxes.
# For a machine that needs them — a Linux desktop without the Debian package,
# or Windows — `scripts/fetch-fonts.sh --with-cjk` adds the four below. They
# are per-language on purpose: one pan-CJK font is what EmulationStation ships
# and is exactly the thing that draws Japanese titles in Chinese shapes.
# All SIL Open Font License 1.1, which permits redistribution as long as the
# licence travels with the font — hence OFL.txt below, and hence LICENSES.md.
# Pinned to a tag, not a branch: a font that changes under a release is a
# layout that changes under a release.
# name
NotoSans[wdth,wght].ttf
NotoSansArabic[wdth,wght].ttf
NotoSansHebrew[wdth,wght].ttf
NotoSansThai[wdth,wght].ttf
OFL.txt
# --with-cjk only. Sizes are why.
[cjk]
NotoSansJP[wght].ttf
NotoSansSC[wght].ttf
NotoSansTC[wght].ttf
NotoSansKR[wght].ttf
